title: Anticholinergic Toxicity: Recognition and Management Principles
subject: Pharmacology
preview: Anticholinergic toxicity may cause dry skin, mydriasis, tachycardia, urinary retention, hyperthermia and delirium.
quickRevision: Anticholinergic toxicity may cause dry skin, mydriasis, tachycardia, urinary retention, hyperthermia and delirium.
Supportive care, temperature control, ECG assessment and toxicology advice guide management.
Physostigmine has selected indications and contraindications; it is not a universal antidote for all unknown poisonings.

sections.title: Pathophysiology & identification
points: Anticholinergic toxicity may cause dry skin, mydriasis, tachycardia, urinary retention, hyperthermia and delirium.
Cholinergic toxicity more often produces excess secretions, lacrimation, bronchorrhea and diarrhea.

sections.title: Diagnostic and treatment connections
points: Supportive care, temperature control, ECG assessment and toxicology advice guide management.
Physostigmine has selected indications and contraindications; it is not a universal antidote for all unknown poisonings.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Dry versus wet secretions can be a useful discriminator, but mixed ingestions are common.

quiz.question: Which feature supports anticholinergic rather than cholinergic toxicity?
quiz.explanation: Dry skin and urinary retention. Anticholinergic toxicity may cause dry skin, mydriasis, tachycardia, urinary retention, hyperthermia and delirium.
